media_type_map.4,5: h263 or built-in ARM callbacks when available

loader_sequence: read OS_INT, OS_EXT and codec files; each fallback path is tried before the ROM path
parse OS_EXT with mode argument 0 and keep its selected entry
start CEVA and wait up to 30 polling iterations, delaying 10 OEM time units per iteration
send command bytes 81 01 00 00 and wait up to 30 polling iterations
parse/copy the codec image with mode argument 0x10
optionally free the three aligned file buffers when context flag bit 0 is set

start_register_writes.0x9053200c: zeroed; later polled for ready-state transition

ceva_command_contract.synchronization: OEM code masks IRQ/FIQ around a CP15 cache-drain/synchronization sequence before mailbox publication

registers.0x90532034: ARM response pointer for a CEVA-to-ARM command
registers.0x9053203c: CEVA reply pointer; OEM returns pointer OR 0x10000000
registers.0x90532048: interrupt mask; helper functions atomically set or clear selected bits
registers.0x9053204c: interrupt status/acknowledge; read for pending bits and written to acknowledge them

interrupt.isr: 0x00349f48 reads status, increments per-bit pending counters, acknowledges bits and returns 2
interrupt.dsr: 0x00349fbc signals reply event bit 1 and wakes the command dispatcher from the pending counters

reply_wait.polling_mode: busy-waits for status bit 0x08 and acknowledges it
reply_wait.rtos_mode: waits for event bit 1 with an absolute deadline of current time + 0x0bb8 OEM time units
reply_wait.result: reads the pointer from 0x9053203c and maps it through the 0x10000000 alias

piu_reply_irq_contract.handler_table: 0x0055b7e0; all 256 entries checked, only opcodes 0x40..0x46 are populated
piu_reply_irq_contract.response_path: handler publishes its ARM response pointer through 0x90532034, performs cache synchronization and acknowledges/notifies status bit 0x02
piu_reply_irq_contract.ownership_note: The original has one synchronous reply path plus a permanent CEVA-to-ARM command dispatcher; buffers and callbacks are shared global state.

safety: Static exact-build analysis only; no firmware or IMG code was executed.
The OEM codec path passes parser modes 0/0x10, so MMPi checksum words are not authenticated there.
The wait-ready code reads 0x9053200c; no SPMP-OS code should touch this image-specific MMIO before board validation.
Several OEM timeout/error branches can deliberately spin forever under debug flags; a new provider must replace them with bounded failures.
The PIU ISR/DSR and 0x10000000 pointer alias are exact-build observations, not a portable address map or permission to install an SPMP-OS interrupt handler.
Paths under /fat20a2/hda2/xyz are OEM development fallbacks, not the user SD layout selected for SPMP-OS.
